name: The Food Movement Natural Products Company
old_description: Founded in 2011, The Food Movement Co. has been dedicated to bringing pure, plant-based nutrition to people worldwide. Every product we make is third-party tested and crafted with care — ensuring quality, integrity, and results you can trust.
about:
The Food Movement Natural Products Company was founded in 2011 in Arlington Heights, Illinois. The company began with a mission to deliver pure, plant-based nutrition to a global audience, emphasizing ingredients sourced from the earth and validated by science. No founders are named in public materials, and the ownership structure has not been disclosed.

The company formulates and sells a range of dietary supplements under the Black Earth® brand, including fulvic and humic mineral concentrates, zeolite detox sprays, colloidal silver, magnesium complexes, and a line of organic superfoods such as Irish sea moss, maca, moringa, and plant-based vitamin C. All products are manufactured without synthetic fillers, use vegan capsules, and undergo third‑party laboratory testing for heavy metals and microbiological contamination. The brand reports distribution through more than 1,000 health‑food stores nationwide and a direct‑to‑consumer channel serving over 10,000 customers.

Primary customers include independent health‑food retailers, specialty grocers, and individual consumers seeking clean‑label supplements. The product categories target energy and vitality, daily balance, whole‑body support, and detoxification. The company also offers a subscription program for recurring deliveries.

The Food Movement differentiates itself by combining regenerative organic and biodynamic plant nutrition with rigorous third‑party verification. Its Black Earth® mineral complex supplies over 70 trace minerals, and the company states that sustainable sourcing from ethical farms and eco‑friendly packaging are core to its founding purpose.

name: The Food Processing Center
old_description: The Food Processing Center is a multi-disciplinary resource for the food industry, providing a combination of consulting, educational, technical, and business development services. We provide a wide range of customizable services, all delivered in a confidential, price-competitive, and timely manner.
about:
The Food Processing Center operates in Lincoln, Nebraska, as a university-affiliated resource within the University of Nebraska system. While its exact founding date is not publicly stated, the center was established to serve as a multi-disciplinary hub for the food industry, drawing on academic expertise to support commercial innovation.

The center delivers a blend of consulting, education, technical assistance, and business development services. Its facilities include a microbiology laboratory equipped for pathogen testing, along with pilot-scale processing capabilities such as extrusion, freeze drying, and high pressure processing (HPP). Staff support product and process development across categories including ice cream, biobased products, and general food formulation, and also offer food safety plan development and food defense planning.

Clients range from startup entrepreneurs to established food manufacturers seeking reformulation, safety validation, or scale-up support. The center serves the broader food processing sector, providing confidential, fee-based services tailored to each project.

The center emphasizes its staff expertise and the integration of research-grade equipment with commercial practicality, positioning itself as a single point of access for technical, regulatory, and commercialization challenges.

The Furniture Ranch serves residential customers across Arizona and surrounding states, working directly with homeowners and designers to create made-to-order pieces. Its showroom and workshop cater to clients seeking personalized furniture for homes, including custom cabinetry for kitchens and bathrooms.

The company emphasizes its family-owned heritage, 25-plus years of experience, and a commitment to unique custom designs as key differentiators. The 10-year guarantee reflects confidence in the durability of its handcrafted solid-wood construction.

name: The Modern Table Company
old_description: The Modern Table Company was founded in 2014 to create unique products for clients looking for eye-catching, one-of-a-kind pieces to enhance their homes. We use reclaimed, repurposed, and new materials to design works of art.
about:
The Modern Table Company was founded in 2014 in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, to create unique, eye-catching furniture pieces for clients seeking one-of-a-kind items to enhance their homes. The company operates from a workshop on North Main Street in the Fox Valley region.

The shop produces custom tables and furniture using reclaimed, repurposed, and new wood that is kiln-dried for durability. Materials include domestic species such as oak, ash, hickory, maple, pine, Douglas fir, cypress, and redwood reclaimed from old Wisconsin pickling vats, as well as the rare Australian jarrah. Each piece is handcrafted to order, with the facility serving both walk-in and appointment-based clients during weekday business hours.

The company serves residential customers and interior designers looking for personalized, sustainable furniture. Projects range from coffee tables and high-top tables with stools to other custom builds tailored to individual specifications. The business emphasizes a collaborative design process that translates client concepts into functional works of art.

The Modern Table Company distinguishes itself through its curated selection of reclaimed woods, each carrying a distinct history, and its commitment to sustainable sourcing. The limited availability of materials like jarrah, brought to the U.S. in 1900, underscores the exclusivity of each commission.

name: The Sweet Life Kettle Corn Company
old_description: family-owned garden center and farm market serving Southern Maine since 1949. Highland Farm offers locally sourced fruits and vegetables, specialty foods, baked goods, plants, and gardening supplies, all grown with environmentally friendly practices.
about:
The Sweet Life Kettle Corn Company operates from Farmington, Maine, where it was established in 1949 as a family-owned enterprise. The business was founded by Jodi Cordes on the premise of producing handcrafted gourmet popcorn while creating meaningful employment for local high school students. What began as a passion for kettle corn has evolved into a mission-driven operation that balances snack production with youth development.

The company produces four core kettle corn varieties—Blue Sky Blueberry, Tall Pines Pumpkin Spice, Coastal Cinnamon Crunch, and the original "ME Bag" Hand Popped Kettle Corn—in small batches using all-natural ingredients. Each 4.5- to 5.5-ounce bag is hand-popped with popcorn, pure cane sugar, oil, salt, and natural flavorings such as blueberries, vanilla, cinnamon, or pumpkin spice. The facility turns out gluten-free, dairy-free, non-GMO, and vegan-friendly snacks that ship within one to three business days.

Products reach consumers through the company's e-commerce site, a growing network of Maine retailers, community events, and fundraising partnerships. The customer base spans individual snack buyers, gift purchasers, event organizers, and organizations seeking mission-aligned fundraising options. Every sale directly funds flexible work shifts for students who juggle academics, athletics, and extracurriculars.

Cordes started the venture to give teenagers real-world experience in customer service, teamwork, and entrepreneurship. The "purpose behind every bag" model means each purchase underwrites skill-building wages for young workers, tying the brand's growth to community impact rather than scale alone.

about:
The Urban Wood Company was founded in 2021 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The business began as a supplier of premium kiln-dried live edge slabs, dimensional lumber, and reclaimed wood, and has since expanded into a full-service custom furniture and cabinetry shop.

The company operates what it describes as the largest vacuum kiln in the state alongside a fully equipped woodshop. Its sawmill capabilities include an on-site bandsaw mill with a 26-inch by 21-foot cutting capacity and an off-site mill capable of 58-inch by 18-foot cuts. Services span custom furniture design, milling, slab flattening, and wood drying, producing items such as live edge tables, river tables, conference tables, kitchen cabinetry, bathroom vanities, storage systems, and architectural millwork.

The shop serves both residential and commercial clients, including homeowners, designers, and contractors seeking high-end custom pieces. Testimonials reference individual customers ordering floating shelves, dining tables, and slab selections for personal projects, while the commercial side addresses office conference tables and similar installations.

The company emphasizes its end-to-end control from slab to finish, highlighting the vacuum kiln for stable, dry lumber and the precision of its milling and woodshop operations. Customer feedback consistently points to knowledgeable staff and responsive service as distinguishing factors.

name: The Wire Guy Electric
old_description: Steven founded The Wire Guy Electric in 2017, bringing over 10 years of experience to serve his community as a trusted resource. In his free time, he enjoys cooking, spending time with his partner Emma and their dog Lulu, watching movies, and doing projects around their home.
about:
The Wire Guy Electric was founded in 2017 by Steven Taylor in Mesa, Arizona. A family-owned operation from the start, Taylor brought over a decade of field experience to serve the Phoenix Valley with a team that now includes his partner Emma Woolington as office manager, service manager Cody Taylor, and a handful of technicians and apprentices. The company maintains two locations — one in Mesa and another in Scottsdale — and operates under Arizona ROC license #365306.

The firm provides a full range of electrical installation, repair, and maintenance services for both residential and commercial customers. Residential work spans new-construction wiring for custom homes, casitas, and additions; panel replacements and service upgrades coordinated with APS and SRP; EV charger installations (Tesla Wall Connector, ChargePoint, NEMA 14-50); recessed and custom lighting; kitchen and bath remodel circuits; and troubleshooting of faults from dead outlets to burning smells. Commercial services include tenant-improvement build-outs for general contractors and property managers, LED retrofits (high-bay, troffer, parking-lot), storefront and sign lighting, dedicated equipment circuits, emergency/exit lighting testing, and off-hours service for retail, office, restaurant, medical, and warehouse facilities.

Customers range from homeowners in communities such as Eastmark, Las Sendas, and Dobson Ranch to commercial property managers overseeing build-outs in Scottsdale’s DC Ranch or Phoenix’s Biltmore corridor. The company bids commercial TI work from plans, phases occupied-building lighting upgrades, and sizes circuits from equipment nameplates for kitchens, medical suites, and server rooms.

The Wire Guy Electric emphasizes transparent flat-rate pricing, a “no BS” quote policy, and a satisfaction guarantee that promises return visits if issues arise. The founders frame the business as a neighborhood resource — born and raised in Mesa — with a combined 30-plus years of trade experience across the team.

old_description: Thornton Plastics specializes in small plastic containers and jars. about:
Thornton Plastics operates from Salt Lake City, Utah, where it was founded in 1955 by Wayne Thornton. The business remains family-owned, with the third generation now the company after more than six decades in operation.

The company manufactures a range of small plastic containers, including snap-cap vials, hinged-lid containers, hinged boxes, and plastic jars with lids. Production uses polystyrene, polypropylene, and polyethylene (including high-density polyethylene), and the firm also distributes hundreds of related packaging items. All manufacturing takes place in the United States, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Thornton Plastics serves the food industry and a variety of other sectors that use hinged-lid containers for packaging, shipping, storing, and sampling. Customers range from individual buyers to commercial accounts, with the company shipping orders as small as a 10-pack up to multiple pallets directly to the end user.

The company emphasizes direct-to-customer sales, highlighting its customer service and willingness to ship any order size. It also points to continuous product innovation and an expanding catalog as reasons customers choose them, along with the fact that everything is made domestically.

name: Thyssenkrupp Automotive Systems of America
old_description: As a publicly listed company, thyssenkrupp is part of the MDAX index. thyssenkrupp shares are traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: TKA) and as American depositary receipts (ticker symbol: TKAMY) in the USA. Since 20 October 2025, TKMS (Marine Systems segment) has also been an independent, publicly traded company in which thyssenkrupp AG holds a majority stake of 51 per cent; TKMS shares are traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: TKMS) and will be included in the MDAX from 22 December 2025.
about:
Thyssenkrupp Automotive Systems of America operates from Chattanooga, Tennessee, as part of the publicly traded thyssenkrupp AG, which is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and included in the MDAX index. The division traces its roots to the broader thyssenkrupp group’s automotive technology activities, though a specific founding year for the U.S. entity is not publicly disclosed. Ownership remains with the German parent company, and no individual founders are named for this subsidiary.

The company supplies high‑tech components and services to the automotive sector, covering drivetrain, undercarriage, body, and steering systems. Its portfolio includes forged and machined parts such as crankshafts, camshafts, cylinder head modules, damping systems, springs, stabilizers, and complete drive and battery assemblies. It also provides production systems for powertrain and battery lines, integrated car‑body solutions, engine and axle assembly, and development of electromechanical steering systems. The Chattanooga location employs approximately 28,892 people across the automotive technology segment, though facility size and annual volumes are not specified.

Customers are primarily automotive OEMs and tier‑1 suppliers in the passenger‑vehicle and commercial‑vehicle markets, as well as manufacturers of construction machinery. The company’s components serve chassis, body, and powertrain applications, with specific references to undercarriage systems, steering gears, and battery assembly for electric vehicles.

Thyssenkrupp highlights its steer‑by‑wire development approach, the use of artificial neural networks to improve steering‑gear quietness, and the cloud‑based IoT platform carValoo for real‑time fleet monitoring as key differentiators. The division positions itself as an integrated partner for production systems and component innovation.

name: Tick Tock Energy, Inc.
old_description: The ITC has existed since 2005 via the federal government and is an offset of tax liability.  Up to 30% solar tax credit is available with potential 10% bonus adders available for sites in an “energy community” or another 10% when a certain percentage of the solar equipment is made of US manufactured domestic content.
about:
Tick Tock Energy, Inc. is based in Effingham, Illinois, and was formed in 2006 by brothers Craig, Eric, and Matt Pals. The venture grew out of a family electrical contracting legacy: their father Mike founded Pals Electric, Inc. in 1983, and Eric brought a decade of experience as a journeyman electrician and IBEW Local 146 project foreman, while Craig contributed a background in energy-efficiency project development for Sempra Energy Solutions (now Honeywell) as a licensed professional engineer.

The company designs and installs solar photovoltaic systems for commercial, agricultural, and residential customers, specializing in ground-mounted arrays — fixed, single-axis, and dual-axis trackers — as well as roof-mounted installations. It also provides long-term operations and maintenance (O&M) services, energy consulting, energy management systems, and energy-efficient lighting retrofits. Since its founding, Tick Tock Energy has installed more than 1 megawatt of solar and small-wind capacity and has reduced several megawatts of electrical demand through lighting and other efficiency measures.

Its client base spans commercial businesses, grain and livestock farms, homeowners, non-profit organizations, and public facilities across Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Iowa, and Kentucky. Notable projects include a 281.6 kW roof-mounted system for a grain farm in McLean, a 700 kW commercial roof array for a refrigerated warehouse in Effingham, a 604.44 kW ground-mounted installation at a rock quarry in Tuscola, and smaller residential arrays for customers served by Ameren and Wayne-White Electric Cooperative.

The founders frame the business around energy independence, arguing that on-site generation shields customers from rising utility costs and inflation. The company assists clients in capturing federal investment tax credits, Illinois Solar Renewable Energy Credits (SRECs), and USDA REAP grants for rural operations.
